# mangos-extractor vessel list: <mapId> <displayId>   # name (entry N)
#
# Each line gives one vessel map the id of the hull model to bake into it.
#
# Generated by joining four_world.transports against gameobject_template (for the display id)
# and against Map.dbc's Directory column, matching "Transport<entry>" EXACTLY -- the same
# comparison Transport::RegisterVesselMap makes. A row that matches keeps the client's own map
# id; everything else is minted as VESSEL_MAP_BASE + entry (1000000 + entry) and tagged below.
# If those two ever disagree the baker writes w_<id>.tile for a map the server never asks for,
# and the ship sails with no deck.
#
# Map.dbc ALSO has rows named for a ROUTE -- Transport_Menethil_Valgarde (612),
# Transport_Moa'ki_Kamagua (621), Transport_Orgrimmar_to_Thunderbluff (647) and eight more.
# Those ids exist and are deliberately NOT used, for two reasons:
#
#   - A route is not a vessel. 206328 "Krazzworks to Dragonmaw Port" and 206329 the other way
#     are one run in two directions -- same period, same display, two entries. Keyed on a route
#     row they would share one deck map: two hulls, one set of coordinates.
#   - It is not a 1:1 keying anyway. Entry 186238 has BOTH Transport186238 (592) and
#     Transport_Orgrimmar_Warsong_Hold (613), and five of the route rows match no transport at
#     all (the BG airships, the Siege of Orgrimmar pair).
#
# Nothing is lost by minting: NO transport row in Map.dbc has client terrain -- 0 of 49, against
# a bake that produced geometry for every ordinary map around them. The hull only ever existed
# as a game object model, so the baker fills the deck from go_<displayId>.tile either way, and
# the map id never goes on the wire.
#
# 27 vessels: 12 matched, 15 minted.
